+# finviz-rea
+
+A standalone, clean-room stock screener with a Charts tab, built for Arman.
+Inspired by the behaviour of commercial screeners; it contains no third-party code, assets or logos.
+
+Status: **Phase 0 (spike and decisions).** No app code yet.
+
+- Plan and phases: see `PROGRESS.md`, and the Phase 0 findings in `docs/PHASE0.md`.
+- Verified free-tier limits with source links: `docs/LIMITS.md`.
+- Raw data samples used for measurements: `docs/samples/`.
+- CPU benchmarks: `scripts/bench/` (run with `node scripts/bench/run.mjs`).
+
+Planned stack: Cloudflare Pages (static files plus Functions), one R2 bucket for the nightly snapshot,
+GitHub Actions for data jobs, Alpaca market data (free plan) with a Yahoo backup.
+Plain readable ES modules; no bundler and no minified code.
+
+Access is through the Arman hub sign-in only (no separate login).
+
+Never commit secrets. Keys go into GitHub or Cloudflare Pages secrets.

+# Verified free-tier limits
+
+Checked on **2026-10-21** by fetching the official pages with `curl` (the Cloudflare pages carry their own "last updated" date).
+"Plan said" is what PLAN.md section 9 assumed from memory.
+
+## Cloudflare Workers / Pages Functions (Workers Free plan)
+
+Source: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/ (also checked https://developers.cloudflare.com/pages/functions/pricing/, https://developers.cloudflare.com/pages/platform/limits/)
+
+| Item | Verified value | Plan said | Notes |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| Requests | **100,000 / day**, resets at 00:00 UTC; error 1027 beyond (fail open or closed per setting) | 100,000/day | Pages Functions share this account-wide quota with Workers. Static asset requests (not invoking a Function) are **free and unlimited**. |
+| CPU time per HTTP request | **10 ms** | ~10 ms | Waiting on `fetch`, R2, KV, cache does not count. Docs: average Worker ~2.2 ms; parsing large payloads typically 10-20 ms. Over the limit gives error 1102. |
+| Memory | 128 MB per isolate | n/a | 2.5 MB snapshot + a few MB of bars is fine. |
+| Subrequests per invocation | **50** (external `fetch`, R2, KV, D1 and so on) | 50 | Internal-service subrequests: 1,000. |
+| Cache API calls per request | **50** (`put`/`match`/`delete`), **shared with the 50 subrequests** per the docs ("same quota as subrequests") | not known | Planned 8 tickers: 1 upstream + 8 match + 8 put = 17. OK. Cache max object 512 MB. |
+| Duration | no hard wall-clock limit while the client is connected; `waitUntil` up to 30 s after response | n/a | |
+| Pages: files / file size | 20,000 files, 25 MiB per file | n/a | Irrelevant here. |
+| Pages: builds | 500 / month (Git-integrated builds only) | n/a | We deploy with `wrangler pages deploy` from Actions, so no Pages build minutes. |
+| Pages: projects | 100 per account (first 48 h of an account have a creation throttle) | n/a | 10+ projects exist now. |
+
+## Cache API
+
+Source: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/cache/
+
+- **Pages Functions have functional Cache API operations on both custom domains and `*.pages.dev`** (explicit sentence in the docs). The plan's worry is resolved on paper; confirm with a live probe in Phase 1 (`X-Cache` header).
+- The cache is **per data centre, not replicated**; entries are evictable.
+- **`stale-while-revalidate` and `stale-if-error` are NOT supported by `cache.put` / `cache.match`.** The plan's "SWR" must be implemented by hand: store `fetchedAt` in a header and decide freshness in code, refreshing with `ctx.waitUntil`.
+- `cache.put` only accepts GET keys, no 206, no `Vary: *`; responses with `Set-Cookie` are not stored; `Cache-Control` on the stored response sets the TTL.
+- Not available for Workers behind Cloudflare Access or in dashboard previews (not our case).
+
+## Cloudflare R2
+
+Source: https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/pricing/ (updated 2026-10-01)
+
+| Item | Verified (Standard storage, free tier, per month) | Plan said |
+|---|---|---|
+| Storage | **10 GB-month** | 10 GB |
+| Class A (writes, lists, copy, multipart) | **1,000,000** | 1,000,000 |
+| Class B (reads, head) | **10,000,000** | 10,000,000 |
+| Egress | **free** (also via Workers API and S3 API) | free |
+| Deletes, abort multipart | **free** | free |
+| Infrequent Access class | not in free tier | n/a (we use Standard) |
+
+- Unauthorized (401) requests are not charged.
+- A card on file: the pricing page does not say. **Evidence from this account: two R2 buckets already exist (`devin-wiki-rewrites`, `drawdown-history`), so R2 is enabled here and no new payment step is expected.**
+
+## Cloudflare KV
+
+Source: https://developers.cloudflare.com/kv/platform/limits/ and /kv/platform/pricing/
+
+| Item | Verified (Free) | Plan said |
+|---|---|---|
+| Reads | **100,000 / day** | 100,000/day |
+| Writes (different keys) | **1,000 / day**; same key 1 per second | 1,000/day |
+| Deletes | 1,000 / day | n/a |
+| List requests | 1,000 / day | n/a |
+| Storage | 1 GB per account/namespace | n/a |
+| Value size | 25 MiB | n/a |
+| Ops per Worker invocation | 1,000 | n/a |
+
+Dashboard and wrangler operations count as usage. Plan unchanged: **zero KV writes for data.**
+
+## GitHub Actions
+
+Sources: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/managing-billing-for-your-products/about-billing-for-github-actions and https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows
+
+| Item | Verified | Plan said |
+|---|---|---|
+| Standard GitHub-hosted runners in **public** repos | **free** | unlimited for public |
+| GitHub Free private repos | **2,000 minutes / month**, 500 MB artifact storage, 10 GB cache | 2,000 |
+| Scheduled workflows | run on the default branch only; **in a public repo they are disabled automatically after 60 days without repository activity** | 60 days |
+| Schedule delay | can be delayed under high load; **load peaks at the start of every hour and queued jobs may be dropped**, so avoid `:00` | not known |
+| Shortest schedule | 5 minutes | n/a |
+| **New:** time zone in cron | an IANA `timezone` can be given for a schedule (DST-aware; skipped hours advance to the next valid time) | not known |
+
+Consequences: the repo is public (Arman's decision), so minutes are not a concern. Schedule the jobs at odd minutes (for example `:17`, `:43`), use the IANA time zone `America/New_York` so DST needs no manual shift, and have the nightly job make a trivial commit or the Pages deploy run at least every few weeks to avoid the 60-day pause (or document the manual re-enable).
+
+## Alpaca Market Data (free "Basic" plan)
+
+Sources: https://docs.alpaca.markets/docs/about-market-data-api, https://docs.alpaca.markets/docs/market-data-faq, https://docs.alpaca.markets/reference/stockbars
+
+| Item | Verified | Plan said

+# Phase 0 results (2026-10-21)
+
+Scope of this run: verify limits, test a data source with a handful of calls, measure CPU, check credentials read-only. No app code, no deploy, no repo on GitHub, no bucket, no hub change.
+
+## Go / no-go summary
+
+| Gate | Verdict | One line |
+|---|---|---|
+| CPU | **GO, with two design changes** | `/api/bars` normalize fits if a call carries at most ~2,800 bars (8 tickers x 350 bars, ~3 ms median) or 4 tickers x 640 bars (~2.8 ms). The snapshot **must** be the binary format (~2 ms); plain JSON (~15 ms) is out. |
+| Data source | **CONDITIONAL GO** | Alpaca free plan facts are confirmed from the docs, but **no Alpaca keys are on the box**, so Alpaca itself is untested. The Yahoo fallback works today (all 7 calls OK, full 04:00-20:00 ET coverage). Phase 1 can start with the Yahoo adapter and add Alpaca when keys arrive. |
+| Limits | **GO** | Every figure in PLAN section 9 checked against official docs; none is worse than assumed. Three corrections (below). |
+| Credentials | **GO for repo + Pages + R2 binding work, with notes** | `gh` can create the repo (`repo`, `workflow` scopes). `CLOUDFLARE_PAGES_TOKEN` is valid and lists Pages projects, but cannot read the account list or R2/KV. `CF_R2_TOKEN` (found in the environment) lists accounts, R2 buckets, KV and Workers; R2 is already enabled on the account. Bucket creation and Pages deploy were not tried (read-only run). |
+
+## 1. Limits (details and URLs in `LIMITS.md`)
+
+Everything the plan marked **[verify]** matched, except:
+
+1. **`cache.put`/`cache.match` do not support `stale-while-revalidate` / `stale-if-error`.** The plan's SWR has to be hand-written (freshness timestamp in a header, refresh through `ctx.waitUntil`).
+2. **Cache API calls count toward the same 50-per-request quota as subrequests.** The planned 8-ticker call (1 upstream + 8 match + 8 put = 17) is still fine; a 44-ticker single call would not be (88).
+3. **Alpaca `limit` (max 10,000) is a total across all symbols and results are sorted by symbol first**, so one page may hold only the first symbols. The adapter must always set `limit=10000`, bound `start`, and follow `next_page_token`.
+
+New useful facts: GitHub cron supports an IANA `timezone` (no manual DST shift) and schedules are dropped/delayed around the top of the hour (use odd minutes); Pages Functions have a working Cache API on `*.pages.dev`; R2 is already enabled on this account (two buckets exist), so the "card on file" worry is moot here.
+
+## 2. Data-source test
+
+`ALPACA_API_KEY_ID` / `ALPACA_API_SECRET_KEY` are **not set**, so per the standing rules the Yahoo chart endpoint was used. 7 calls total (limit was ~20), made from this box; the endpoint answered 200 every time.
+
+Samples (raw JSON, no secrets) are in `docs/samples/`:
+
+| Sample | Interval/range | Bytes | Time | Bars | Null bars | Zero-volume bars |
+|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
+| AAPL | 5m / 5d | 60,130 | 0.17 s | 949 | 0 | 561 |
+| F | 5m / 5d | 54,729 | 0.15 s | 822 | 0 | 432 |
+| NCPL | 5m / 5d | 56,936 | 0.16 s | 949 | 1 | 562 |
+| QS | 5m / 5d | 49,678 | 0.15 s | 758 | 0 | 368 |
+| STAK (thin) | 5m / 5d | 32,122 | 0.14 s | 496 | **142** | 251 |
+| AAPL | 1m / 5d | 261,377 | 0.18 s | 4,057 | 0 | 2,102 |
+| QS | 1m / 5d | 201,291 | 0.15 s | 2,759 | 1 | 806 |
+
+Findings:
+- **Fields:** `chart.result[0]` has `meta` (32 keys including `regularMarketTime`, `chartPreviousClose`, `previousClose`, `exchangeTimezoneName`, `currentTradingPeriod.{pre,regular,post}`, `tradingPeriods`, `longName`), `timestamp[]` (epoch seconds) and `indicators.quote[0].{open,high,low,close,volume}`. About 65 bytes per bar of JSON.
+- **Extended hours: yes.** With `includePrePost=true` every liquid ticker has bars from 04:00 to 19:55-19:59 ET on all 5 sessions (the last bar on a day is stamped at the last tick, for example 19:59). The sessions line up with the plan's 04:00-20:00 grid.
+- **Gap handling differs by liquidity.** Liquid and mid names come back already gap-filled (about half of the bars are zero-volume carry-forward bars); the thin name STAK has 142 of 496 bars with `null` OHLC and starts as late as 05:00 on some days. The adapter must treat `null` as "no trade" (same as an absent Alpaca bar) and the client does its own carry-forward fill.
+- **No 3-minute interval.** 1m covers about 5-8 days, so a 3M chart means aggregating 1m (200-260 KB per ticker for 5 days, so 44 tickers is ~10 MB: only workable in batches or per ticker in the browser, one reason Alpaca stays primary).
+- **One ticker per call**, ~0.15 s each from this box. 44 tickers = 44 calls (and the Pages subrequest limit is 50). Fine as an emergency fallback only.
+- **Delay:** Yahoo's last bar was the 19:59 ET close tick, i.e. effectively real-time. That is *better* than the free Alpaca SIP feed (15 min behind), which makes Yahoo attractive but unofficial; keep it as fallback and note the difference in the UI chip.
+- Alpaca: not called. Latency, payload size, extended-hours coverage and the 3-minute bars are **unverified until keys exist**.
+
+## 3. CPU measurement (`scripts/bench/`, `node scripts/bench/run.mjs 500`)
+
+Method: Node 20 on an 8-core Xeon (not Workers). Fixtures are built from the recorded samples (`fixtures.mjs`): Alpaca-shaped JSON (`{"bars":{"SYM":[{c,h,l,n,o,t,v,vw}]}}`, trade bars only, aggregated to 3 minutes) replicated to N symbols, and a fake 5,600-row snapshot with 70 float32 columns. 500 iterations each; the table is the median of two full runs (full output in `docs/bench-output.txt`; single runs vary by about 10-15 %).
+
+`/api/bars` step = `JSON.parse` + per-bar normalize (ISO date to epoch, rounding, session volume, regular close) + `JSON.stringify` per ticker:
+
+| Payload | JSON size | Parse only | + normalize | + stringify (what a miss costs) | p95 | Max seen |
+|---|---|-

+## Alpaca verification (run 2, 2026-10-22 04:46 UTC, after hours)
+
+Three calls, all HTTP 200, headers `APCA-API-KEY-ID` / `APCA-API-SECRET-KEY` (values never logged). Samples in `docs/samples/alpaca_*.json`.
+
+| Call | Latency | Size | Result |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| 3Min, feed=sip, end = now-16 min, 5 symbols (STAK NCPL QS AAPL F), 5 days, limit=10000 | 0.31 s | 374 KB | AAPL 947, F 760, NCPL 932, QS 743, STAK 349 bars; 04:00-19:57 ET incl. pre/post; no `next_page_token` |
+| 3Min, feed=iex, same | 0.27 s | 138 KB | AAPL 391, F 395, QS 363, NCPL 218, STAK 24 bars: **IEX is far too thin for small caps** (STAK 24 vs 349) |
+| 1Day, feed=sip, 5 symbols, 30 days | 0.23 s | 11.6 KB | 22 bars per symbol, includes the current day's bar |
+
+Findings: SIP with an end bound of now-16 min works on the free plan; `3Min` native; ~100 B per bar raw JSON (~40 B after normalizing to columnar arrays). Bars exist only where trades happened (thin tickers have gaps; the renderer must handle missing slots). IEX is only for the Phase 5 real-time tail. Daily multi-symbol call is cheap: ~2.3 KB per symbol-month, so a 5,600-symbol nightly job is ~100 calls of 50 symbols (well under 200/min).
+
+CPU bench on the Alpaca-shaped payload (`scripts/bench/alpaca_bench.mjs`, 5 symbols x ~750 bars = 3,731 bars): parse + normalize + stringify **median 3.95 ms, p95 5.2 ms** on Node (x2 for Workers ~ 8-10 ms): within budget only with the ~3,000-bar cap per call; keep the 8-ticker/3,000-bar rule and keep normalization minimal.

+#!/bin/bash
+# Phase-0 Alpaca probe. Usage: probe.sh <outfile> <url>. Keys come from env, never printed.
+out="$1"; url="$2"
+curl -s -o "$out" -w "http=%{http_code} time=%{time_total}s size=%{size_download}B\n" \
+  -H "APCA-API-KEY-ID: $ALPACA_API_KEY_ID" -H "APCA-API-SECRET-KEY: $ALPACA_API_SECRET_KEY" "$url"

diff --git a/scripts/secret_scan.sh b/scripts/secret_scan.sh
new file mode 100755
index 0000000..42082b2
--- /dev/null
+++ b/scripts/secret_scan.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,10 @@
+#!/bin/bash
+# Fails if any tracked/staged file contains a real env secret value or a key-like pattern.
+cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
+bad=0
+for v in ALPACA_API_KEY_ID ALPACA_API_SECRET_KEY CLOUDFLARE_PAGES_TOKEN CF_R2_TOKEN HUB_PASSWORD HUB_GATE_PASSWORD; do
+  val="${!v}"; [ -z "$val" ] && continue
+  if grep -rIlF --exclude-dir=.git --exclude-dir=node_modules -- "$val" . >/dev/null; then echo "SECRET VALUE of $v found in files"; bad=1; fi
+done
+if grep -rIlE --exclude-dir=.git --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude=secret_scan.sh '(AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}|PK[A-Z0-9]{18}|sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{32,})' . >/dev/null; then echo "key-like pattern found"; bad=1; fi
+[ $bad = 0 ] && echo "secret scan clean"; exit $bad
